app.notes:
### Added

- **Button layouts hold everything** (firmware protocol 1.24). The Button layouts you already have now hold, for every button, a **Press**, **Hold** (with its time), **Double press**, **With PS** (pressed together with the PS button), **Toggle** and **Turbo**. Each of them can be a controller button, a keyboard key (with Ctrl / Shift / Alt / Win), a mouse button, mouse movement or the wheel, a layer, the gyro, or nothing (Disabled). A layout also holds up to three **layers** over the base, **Gyro as mouse** (or as the right stick; in the Gyroscope section) and its own **trigger effects** (Tension, below).
- **Layouts on the board work without the app.** **Put on the board** keeps up to 8 layouts on your board, and one of them runs from power-on, with or without the app. The save bar writes them. A game's profile picks a layout that runs while the game does; nothing is saved on your board for it.
- **Keyboard keys just work.** In Button assignments, pick a button (click it, choose it from the list or press it on the controller), then press a key on your PC's keyboard: that key, with Ctrl / Shift / Alt / Win held, becomes the button's Press. Escape un-picks; the Key tab's **Show all keys** covers keys you can't press. There is no switch to find: when you save, the app turns your board's keyboard and mouse on if a layout on the board (or one a game's profile sends) presses a key, uses the mouse or uses the gyro as the mouse, and off when none does. When that changes, your board reconnects by itself and a short notice says so; if it can't, the error says why and Button assignments offers **Reconnect USB**. Without key targets, the USB stays exactly as before. Keys and mouse pause while the app's window is in front, so a key never presses buttons in the app. Not yet tested on every system.
- **Tension: your own adaptive trigger effects** (firmware protocol 1.23). In Adaptive triggers, Tension edits L2 and R2 of the layout you're editing. Per trigger: **Game** (the game's own effect), **Fill in** (yours only while the game sends nothing on that trigger) or **Replace** (always yours), with up to 4 stages, each one of the DualSense's effects (Feedback, Weapon, Vibration, Multiple Position Feedback, Slope Feedback, Multiple Position Vibration; Bow, Galloping and Machine marked unofficial) with its pull window, a hold time, and one setting that can build with the pull or with the time held. A picture shows each trigger's strength over the pull and marks a stage an earlier one cuts short. **Trigger effects: start from** puts in Bow, Heavy trigger, Brake pedal or Machine gun (L2 and R2 only; the buttons stay). **Feel it** runs what you're editing before you save it, and **Tension now** shows what runs on each trigger, live. Your board runs the effects itself, with or without the app.
- **The Waveshare RP2350B-Plus-W is a known board.** A board running the firmware built for it (firmware PR #27, built by hand for now) shows as RP2350B-Plus-W with its specs on your board's page (RP2350B, 2× Cortex-M33, 520 KB SRAM, 16 MB flash, CYW43439, Bluetooth 5.2). No firmware update is offered for it yet, and the app still refuses to write another board's firmware to it.
- **Diagnostics shows what was lost on the way.** On your board's page, Diagnostics has a new **Lost on the way** group with the firmware's loss counters: Bluetooth reports dropped because the output queue was full (BT drop), mic packets and frames dropped and 1 ms gaps in the mic audio (Mic i, Mic b, Mic u), and the PC's speaker audio overruns (USB ovr, a lower bound: it is counted once per check). The names in brackets are the OLED Diagnostics screen's, and each one has an ⓘ. They show with firmware 0.9.5-dev.21 and later; older firmware shows nothing rather than zeros.

### Changed

- **Button assignments opens on the layout you're editing** (with firmware that has button layouts). Pick a button by clicking it on the drawing, choosing it from the **Button** list or pressing it on the controller. Its rows read like sentences, and a picker with **Controller / Key / Mouse / Layer / Gyro** tabs sets what each row does. Changed buttons get a label on the drawing; **Swap with…**, **Reset this button**, layer tabs above the drawing (**+ Layer**), **One hand (left / right)** and **Toggle instead of hold** to start from, and plain warnings (for example when nothing presses ✕ or a Hold delays a button's press). **Live from the board** shows what the PC really got for each press. Each piece shows once your board's firmware has it; with older firmware Button assignments stays as it was and says what to update.

### Fixed

- **macOS: ⌘W closes the window again.** The app's own menu (dev.21) kept the App, Edit and Window menus but left out File, where Close lives, so ⌘W stopped closing the window. The File menu is back with Close (⌘W).
